name: Serbia
system: Unitary parliamentary republic (strong presidency in practice)

governingParties: Students' List expected to form the next government

elections.name: Snap parliamentary election
elections.note: Student-led opposition list defeated Vučić's SNS; turnout reported near record highs. Vučić conceded.

elections.name: Early presidential election (due after Vučić's resignation)

synopsis: In a seismic shift, the student-led opposition movement that grew out of protests over the 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse defeated Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party on 25 October 2026, ending more than a decade of SNS dominance. Vučić, who resigned the presidency in September to run for prime minister, conceded on election night; a new government led by the Students' List is expected once results are certified.
policies: EU accession while managing ties with Russia and China
challenges: Forming a government from a list of political newcomers
A peaceful transfer of power and SNS-aligned institutions
Vacant presidency and early presidential election
Kosovo dispute and NIS oil company sanctions
reviewNote: Results provisional (party projection; official RIK results pending). Confirm seat totals, the acting president's name and the Students' List's PM candidate.
